headline: For an exact source-valid three-heavy-plus-three-diffuse-bank frame with leverage ell in each active direction, the limiting central density is 3sqrt(2)[1-c(u)ell^2+O(ell^3)] uniformly in orientation, with 69/320<=c(u)<=41/160. Thus qualitative nonzero heavy leverage carries no fixed or linear sharp-density penalty near the diffuse obstruction.

theorem.scope: Exact finite matrices with nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}; independent centered unit-interval physical inputs; fixed partial leverage ell with Gaussian diffuse-bank limit; central density asymptotic as ell tends to zero.
theorem.uniformity: The O(ell^3) remainder can be taken uniform over u in S^2; hence there is an absolute ell_0 with p_{ell,u}(0)<3sqrt(2) for all orientations and 0<ell<=ell_0.

partner_applied.application: Used the exact orientation coefficient c(u) from the completed diffuse uniform-bank Edgeworth theorem, then independently rederived its cone contraction and identified ell^2 as the replacement for 1/m via the source characteristic function.

Compared the local contiguous-heavy perturbation with the completed rare-fragment barrier: remote m^-2 fragments worsen the first-order deficit, while local heavy leverage has no linear term and starts at ell^2.

correction_status: No refuted arbitrary-joint coarea, conditional-density cap/moment, pointwise oscillatory decay, post-rotation independence, or single-minor extraction premise is used. Live correction inbox was reread at the prepublication control commit and did not require retraction.
unresolved_implication: The theorem is central-peak and small-leverage only. It does not exclude an off-zero density maximum above 3sqrt(2) at intermediate leverage, nor prove the full universal upper bound.
next_step: Determine the global output maximum as a function of intermediate leverage ell for genuinely coupled orientations, or construct a finite/mesoscopic off-zero overshoot; this is the bridge between diffuse and saturated endpoint exclusions.
